documents.title: Telehealth follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at her kitchen table, identity verified.

ED record from 12/29 arrived 1/5: right leg 3/5 with increased tone and brisk reflexes, left eye acuity down with APD, labs unremarkable (WBC 7.0, Hgb 13.5, plt 250, Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 0.9, glucose 98), MRI with one enhancing lesion. Discharged to follow up with neurology.

Today: right leg is "coming back", walking around the apartment and to the car without help, slower on stairs. Left eye blur easing. No falls. Bladder as usual with CIC. MS clinic appointment set for later this month. Feeling worn down by how often these are happening; she wants to ask neurology whether interferon is still the right drug.

A/P
1. RRMS relapse 12/2025, right leg and left eye, active lesion. Improving by report. Encouraged her to bring her question about treatment to neurology; I will forward this note.
2. Fall precautions reviewed.
3. Monitoring labs due in March.
In-person visit in spring.

documents.title: Monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC/LFTs unremarkable. Faxed to MS clinic. Pt messaged.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring check-in.

MS: no new symptoms since the December relapse. Walking her usual loop again. Left eye back to what she calls normal for her, right eye still dim at night. Still on interferon beta-1a three times a week; she says the MS clinic is keeping her on it for now. Vitamin D3 daily.
Bladder: CIC twice daily, oxybutynin most days. No infections since last April. Occasional leakage, manageable.
Mood: PHQ-9 4. Busy at work, good support from friends.

Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Right APD. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Walks into the room without assistance, gait steady.

A/P
1. RRMS, relapses 7/2025 and 12/2025, per neurology on interferon beta-1a. Monitoring labs normal in March; next set in the fall with her physical.
2. Neurogenic bladder with urge incontinence on CIC and oxybutynin; oxybutynin refills sent.
3. Right optic neuropathy, history of bilateral optic neuritis; stable.
4. Vitamin D deficiency, on D3.
Physical in October. Message me with any new symptoms.

events.reason: bilateral leg weakness, numbness below the navel, urinary retention

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD, area hospital
Arrival 06/16/2026, 15:10

CC: legs giving out, numb from the belly button down, cannot urinate.

HPI: 33F with relapsing-remitting MS and neurogenic bladder (self-catheterizes), whose last relapse was right leg weakness in December. Both legs have been getting weaker, she has trouble walking and has fallen several times at home. Numb below the navel. Has not been able to void since this morning. Recalls a right-eye blurring episode about two years ago that cleared on its own.

Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA. FH: mother autoimmune hypothyroidism, father hypertension, no MS.

Exam: Strength 2/5 in both lower extremities. Light touch and pinprick reduced below the T6 level. Lower extremity reflexes brisk. Bilateral upgoing toes.

Workup: CBC normal. ESR normal. B12 normal. Aquaporin-4 IgG negative. Lumbar puncture: CSF oligoclonal bands positive.
MRI spinal cord: T2 hyperintense lesion at T4.

Assessment: Acute myelitis at T4 in known MS, with paraparesis, sensory level and urinary retention.

Disposition: Bladder catheter placed for retention. Admitted to the neurology service.

Emergency medicine
Copy to PCP

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital neurology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - neurology inpatient service, area hospital
Admitted 06/16/2026 from the ED. Discharged 06/22/2026.

Principal diagnosis: relapse of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis with acute myelitis at T4.

Hospital course: Admitted with bilateral leg weakness (2/5), a T6 sensory level and urinary retention. MRI showed a T2 lesion at T4; AQP4 antibody negative and CSF oligoclonal bands positive, consistent with MS. Treated with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days, tolerated. Indwelling catheter for retention; removed before discharge, and she resumed intermittent self-catheterization without difficulty. Inpatient physical therapy throughout. By discharge leg strength had improved to 4/5 on both sides and she walked the unit with a rolling walker.

Discharge medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC three times weekly (continued until outpatient neurology review); oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily as needed; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Steroid course completed in hospital, no taper.
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home. Rolling walker. Outpatient physical therapy referral placed.

Follow-up: MS clinic within 2-3 weeks to review disease-modifying therapy. Primary care in 1-2 weeks.

Hospital neurology
cc: primary care, MS clinic

documents.title: Back home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I was in the hospital for almost a week, a big flare in my spinal cord. Had the IV steroids. I'm home now with a walker, PT starts next week. MS clinic appointment is mid-July and they want to talk about switching meds. Cathing on my own again. Not sure if I need to see you or if I can wait till the fall?

documents.title: RE: Back home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Samantha, I'm so sorry you went through that, and thank you for letting me know. I received the hospital summary. I would like to see you in the next couple of weeks, either in person or by video if getting here is hard right now, to go over the hospital stay, your bladder and how you're managing at home. Our front desk will call to set it up. Meanwhile, please call or come in for fever, burning with urination, new weakness or a fall.

documents.title: Scheduling call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called per PCP to schedule post-hospital visit (in person or video). No answer, voicemail left with callback number. Portal message sent as well.

documents.title: Oxybutynin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request oxybutynin 5 mg, 90-day supply. Last office visit 5/15. Approved by PCP. Note on chart: post-hospital visit still not scheduled, second voicemail left today.
